ct a customer's contact details on the customer screen (Story: CRM-68)

---

## Prerequisites

- **CUSTOMERS-7-API (CRM-67)** completed: the `PATCH
/api/v1/customers/:id` route exists, accepts a partial `{ name?, email?, phone? }` body, returns the updated customer, and refuses with `{ code, f
ields: [...] }` on validation / conflict. Contract confirmed against `api/src/features/customers/correct-contacts.test.js

` (see acceptance table below).
- Coordinate with the API owner if the shape of the write's response, or the

`fields` naming inside a refusal, ever needs to change — the frontend depends on both.

---

## Story Goal

On the customer screen the agent can corre
ct a customer's **name**, **email**, and **phone** in place. The screen sends **only the fields that were edited**, patches the page from the write's answer (no
reload), and marks the offending field on a refusal using the shared code sentence. The **Save** control is not off

ered when nothing changed. Every user-visible string is in both language resource files.

Out of scope: any change

under `api/`, deleting a customer, and sending a revision on the write.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `web/src/pages/customers/CustomerScreenPage.tsx`
— **~lines 1–230**. Study how the screen composes `useCustomer(id)`, `useWriteNote(id)`, and `useGr
antSignIn(id)`; how it locally patches state (see `added` at
lines 45–49 and `useEffect(() => setAdded([]), [screen])`); the existing **contacts** card at **lines 86–99
** where the two `<Isolated>` values for `customer.email` / `customer.phone` render — that card is what you

replace with an editable form.

equest<Note>()`, `run(() => request<Note>(...))`, and returning `{ status, error, write }`. Model the new hook on it exactly, one `useRequ

est` per action.

`ApiError` and that `run` throws on failure so callers can `.catch(() => null)` (as `submit` in `CustomerScreenPage.tsx` line 57

does).
4. `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts` — the `ApiError` shape, in particular the **`fields`** property carried on validation refusals. That is what the screen matches against to

decide which field to mark.
5. `web/src/shared/api/client.ts` — the `request<T>` helper used by every hook in this folder. Confirm the method /

headers convention before adding `PATCH`.
6. `web/src/pages/customers/useCustomer.ts` — how the screen state is loaded and relo

aded (`{ status, error, screen, reload }`). The new hook must not need to call `reload`; the write's answer is enough.
7. `web/src/pages/customers/A
ddCustomerPage.tsx` and `useAddCustomer.ts` — a sibling **write** with field-level error mapping and `Field` `error={…

}` usage. Match its structure (no native `type="email"`, no `required` — see L-55 and existing screens).
8. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `
web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — locate the `customerScreen` namespace (it already carries `contacts`, `noEmail`, `noPhone`, `noteLabel`, `noteRequired`, `noteFailed`, et

c.). Add the new keys to both files; the parity test enforces both.

10. `web/src/pages/customers/C
ustomerScreenPage.test.tsx`, `web/src/pages/customers/InternalNote.test.tsx`, `web/src/pages/customers/GrantSignIn.test.tsx` — the rendering /

assertion patterns for tests on this screen (single-request assertion, error sentence assertion, resource-string usage).
11. `api/src/

features/customers/correct-contacts.test.js` — **~lines 45–250**. The contract you plan against:
    - `PATCH /api/v1/customers/:id` with

a partial patch; **untouched fields are not sent**.
    - Success returns the customer (with normalised `email

`, trimmed `phone`, `phone` nullable, etc.).
    - Refusals return `{ code, fields: [...] }` — e.g. `fields: ['email']` for
`VALIDATION` / `CONFLICT` / same address / same-as-existing, `fields: ['name']` when whole-record validation ref

uses, `fields: ['changes']` when the body carried nothing correctable, `404` when the customer is gone.
12. `doc
s/taxonomy.md` and `docs/architecture.md` — cite for folder placement (`web/src/pages/customers/…`) and the shared-h

ook rule.
13. `.squad/plan-lessons.md` — read once before writing code; do not repeat any listed defect (especially: no pnpm, no `--

filter`, no AI attribution in commits / docs, resource-file strings for **both** languages).

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current beh

aviour:** the contacts card on the customer screen only **displays** `email` and `phone`; there is no way to correct them from the app.
- **New behaviour:** the same card
offers an editable name / email / phone form. Save is only enabled and only rendered when at least one field differs from the lo

aded value. The write sends **only** the changed fields, patches the screen from the response, and on refusal marks the offending field(s) using the shared `t.errors[code]` sentence.

## Backend Tasks

**No backend changes required.** `CUSTOMERS-7-API (CRM-67)` owns the route. This story

consumes it.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **No change made.** `changed === false` → the Save button is not rendered at all. Verified in section 2

above; a test in the plan below asserts the button is absent when drafts equal the loaded values.
- **Only one
field edited.** Request body carries exactly one key. The backend contract at `api/src/features/customers/correct-contacts.test.js` **lines 55–86** requ

ires this; the audit `before` / `after` diff key must equal the request key.
- **Clearing the phone.** Draft trimmed to `''` becomes `phone: null
` in the patch (nullable per `api/src/features/customers/correct-contacts.test.js` **lines 212–227**). Clearing name is ref

used server-side with `fields: ['name']` (see **lines 88–98**); the screen marks the name field.
- **Duplicate email (409).** Response

`fields: ['email']`, code `CONFLICT`. The email field is marked with `t.errors.CONFLICT`; the form is not cleared; drafts survive.
- **

Same-as-existing email (409 on self).** `fields: ['email']` (see **lines 137–147**). Same handling as duplicate.
- **Whole-record validation refusal.
** For a corrected field that fails validation the API returns `fields: [<field>]` (see **lines 100–113**); the ex

act field is marked. When the API returns `fields: ['changes']` for an empty patch, the screen must never fire that request because the Save control is hidden — treat any observed `fields: ['changes']` as a def

ect in the diff logic.
- **Customer was deleted while the form was open.** `PATCH` returns `404` (see **lines 229–239**). The screen shows the sh

ared `NOT_FOUND` sentence in an `ErrorState`; no field is marked.
- **Concurrent edits on the same screen.** `useRequest` (see
`web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts` **lines 13–18, 46–50**) uses a monotonic ticket so a stale response cannot repaint after
a newer save. The seeding `useEffect` in section 2 uses `screen` as its dependency, so a re-seed happens exactly when

the loaded customer changes.
- **RTL rendering of the read-only values elsewhere on the screen.** Any remaining places that render

`customer.email` / `customer.phone` outside the form must keep the `<Isolated>` wrap (comment at **lines 89–91**).
- **Non-ASCII names.** Accepted; the form is

a plain text input, no normalization performed client-side.
- **Native browser validators.** Do **not** add `type="email"` or `required` (L-

55): the browser's default message is in the browser's language and outside `t.errors`.

---

request" pattern from `CustomerScreenPage.test.tsx`.

fields: ['email'] }`; assert the email `Field` shows `t.errors.CONFLICT` and the other fields show none.
    - **Multi-field refusal marks all list

ed fields.** `422 VALIDATION` with `fields: ['name', 'phone']`; both fields carry the sentence; the untouched email field does not.
    - **Clearing the phone sends `phone:

null`.** Empty the phone input and save; assert body is `{ phone: null }`.
    - **A `404` after the customer was deleted shows the shared `NOT_FOUND` sentence in an `ErrorState

`, not a field marker.**

3. **Keep green:** `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` (new keys in both `en

.ts` and `ar.ts`) and `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` (no bare strings in `CustomerScreenPage.tsx`).

Do **not** add or edit backend tests; the

API layer is out of scope.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** from `web/`, `npm test` (vitest) — all new + existing suites pass; parity and no-hardcoded-

strings tests green.
2. **Frontend builds:** from `web/`, `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) — the screen and new hook type-check. **The web suite does not typ

echeck under `npm test`; the `build` step is the type-check.**
3. **Regression:** from `web/`, run the whole customers fol

der — `npm test -- src/pages/customers`.
4. **No AI attribution:** from repo root, `grep -r -n -i -E 'cop
ilot|chatgpt|openai|anthropic|claude|cursor|ai[- ]?assist' . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git` retur

ns nothing added by this change.
5. **Manual sanity in dev:** `cd api && npm start` and `cd web && npm run dev`, sign in as an agent, open a
customer, correct one field at a time and verify (a) the screen updates without a full reload, (b) network shows one `PATCH` with only the changed key, (c) refusals

mark the right field with the localized sentence, (d) the Save button disappears when drafts match the loaded values.

---

] A corrected contact detail is visible on the screen without a reload; the write's response drives the update.

never the untouched ones.
- [ ] A refusal that names a field marks that field with the shared `t.errors[code]` sentence; a general failure surfaces an `Err

orState` with the same sentence source.
- [ ] The Save control is not rendered when no field differs from the loaded values.
- [ ] Every user-visible string (`
nameLabel`, `emailLabel`, `phoneLabel`, `contactsSave`, `contactsSaving`, `contactsFailed`, and any newly needed `errors.*`) lives in **

both** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`; `parity.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] No native validators (`type="email"`, `required`) are added to the new

inputs.
- [ ] No `api/` file is touched. No revision field is invented on the write. No delete-customer control is added.
- [ ] `npm test` (web) and `npm
run build` (web) both pass; `npm test` (api) unchanged and still passes.
